answer: Latency nadir gating. Each new identity must route its first N transactions through a shared inlet queue, and only agents whose median response time sits near the network’s measured nadir (lowest sustained latency band) get promoted. Sybils flooding registrations raise queue contention and push their own timings above that band, so each identity pays fresh calibration traffic and delay before earning throughput, while violet-tagged fast lanes stay reserved for proven low-latency peers.
